name: Neptune Petrochemicals Limited
financial_scope: Standalone; group result separately reconciled, no mixing groupcash
price_status: Official historical closing row; not rolling quote
classification: Research hold — unresolved financial reliability and current funding

GOV.rationale: Recurring specific compliance and disclosure weaknesses constrain stewardship; severe minority harm is not established.
supporting_facts: URC1/demat issues and four secretarial exceptions remain material to record quality.
Commercial related-party exposure and two auditor changes require monitoring, not a presumption of abuse.
GOV.counterevidence: Unmodified opinions, no reported default or fraud, disclosed RPTs and resignations expressly denying audit disputes.

MOAT.rationale: Procurement and distribution capability is useful but contestable, with limited proof of sustained pricing or cost advantage.
supporting_facts: Refineries and competing bitumen distributors offer overlapping products; the new license is nonexclusive.
Top-three supplier concentration of 88.25% and an actual March shortage challenge a network-advantage claim.
MOAT.counterevidence: Long predecessor operating history, logistics footprint and large sales demonstrate real execution capability.

REV.rationale: The declared FY23–FY26 reported CAGR of 14.1222% is cross-checked against gross-profit CAGR of 14.8784%. Both map to the 10–15% score-6 band; no trajectory adjustment.
supporting_facts: Four comparable annual observations and a value-added bridge support underlying economic expansion.
Manufacturing/trading mix is disclosed; no material acquired revenue is identified; the distorted FY22 transition base is excluded.
REV.counterevidence: FY24 sales fell and latest half-year growth slowed to 6.32%; the commodity price/volume decomposition is unavailable.

DUR.rationale: Road construction and maintenance offer accessible demand and capacity headroom, but sourcing, financing and competition limit visibility.
supporting_facts: Low historical plant utilization is headroom rather than proof of demand.
Supply disruption and deferred plant expenditure constrain aggressive growth; the new finance venture is unproven.
DUR.counterevidence: Repeated regional operations and spare plant throughput provide some scalable runway.

CAP.rationale: Alternative asset classifications move the incremental NOPAT/capital diagnostic from 7.93% to 17.38%; insufficiently described assets prevent a reliable score.
supporting_facts: Normalized NOPAT rises from ₹9.7348 crore to ₹23.3002 crore between FY23 and FY26.
₹92.9627 crore of other noncurrent assets and ₹37.1443 crore of advances can change the return conclusion against a 12–16% cost-of-capital assumption.
CAP.counterevidence: Positive NOPAT growth and modest physical capex show potentially efficient trading economics.

CASH.rationale: Four-year weak realization, aged receivables and reversible liability funding establish persistent weakness beyond FY26 alone; the GQS ceiling of 5 applies.
supporting_facts: FY23–FY26 CFO/PAT is 4.82%, or 3.28% using the alternative FY24 restated cashflow; before-interest FCF totals negative ₹2.9862 crore.
FY25 liability support of ₹45.44 crore reverses by ₹105.12 crore in FY26; FY25 receivables older than one year are ₹9.78 crore.
CASH.counterevidence: FY24 and FY25 had positive CFO; FY26 released receivables and inventory. An unidentified investing transfer is not labeled an operating loss.

BAL.rationale: Current liquidity and obligations cannot be authenticated while material asset classifications and notes remain unresolved. This is not a fabricated low score or a claimed default.
supporting_facts: Reported cash of ₹10.8933 crore is not necessarily unrestricted, while IPO proceeds of ₹7.3393 crore remain unspent at March end.
Other noncurrent assets and advances dwarf known cash; current bank terms, guarantees and release conditions remain unavailable.
BAL.counterevidence: Gross debt is ₹18.91 crore against book equity of ₹170.40 crore; profitable operations and possible deposits may provide funding.

EXEC.rationale: Delivery is mixed: revenue and operating profit grew and IPO working capital was deployed, while office and plant expenditure was delayed or reallocated.
supporting_facts: ₹17 crore of working capital was accelerated from the originally planned FY27 use.
Original plant expenditure was largely deferred; office completion shifted to March 2027, and supply disruption was disclosed.
EXEC.counterevidence: Shareholders approved the reallocation and monitoring reports explain the changes; this is not evidence of secret diversion.

EARN.rationale: Operating earnings improved, but large other income and dilution weaken recurring per-share profit quality.
supporting_facts: Other income represents 27.37% of PBT; normalized PAT is ₹22.0679 crore against reported ₹30.3390 crore.
PAT rose 20.87% while weighted EPS fell 10.24%; fresh shares expanded the pre-IPO share count by 36.03%.
EARN.counterevidence: FY26 operating EBITDA grew from ₹23.5455 crore to ₹31.7972 crore; PAT growth is not entirely nonoperating.

R.rationale: Ordinary return is withheld under G2/G3. A hypothetical ₹30 crore recovery is not a verified, funded base case.
supporting_facts: The base case without unverified funding breaches its reserve; the hypothetical-release base returns only 5.67%.
The observed price is dated 15 October and execution/current funding remain uncertain.
R.counterevidence: The conditional bull case can fund and produce 26.79%; this does not establish asset availability.

D.rationale: Thin commodity spreads, unknown asset recoverability and SME exit constraints create permanent-loss risk without establishing actual impairment.
supporting_facts: 59.3% of assets require classification before book value can serve as reliable downside support.
Supply interruptions are disclosed and whole-lot execution capacity is very limited.
D.counterevidence: Book equity substantially exceeds debt and the assets may prove fully recoverable.

P.rationale: No ordinary priced-expectation point is assigned until funding and normalization reconcile; the linked reverse case is explicitly conditional.
supporting_facts: Normalized PE of 18.20 differs materially from reported PE.
The conditional 15% hurdle solution requires 22.11% annual revenue growth and an unverified ₹30 crore asset release.
P.counterevidence: Reported PE of 13.24 is not an obviously extreme headline valuation.

L.rationale: Eight absent issuer rows are unclassified, so the complete 60-session distribution cannot be scored. One whole lot exceeds all tested observed-median participation budgets.
supporting_facts: Observed 60-window median turnover is ₹279,200; a smoothed 5% participation exit for ₹5 lakh takes 35.82 sessions before lot constraints.
The 500-share lot costs ₹88,650; observation coverage is 52/60 and 14/20, while spread, depth and historical surveillance are unavailable.
L.counterevidence: 52 authenticated rows and the normal SM series establish some actual trading, not a suspension.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: Recurring statutory exceptions, related-party exposures and disclosure inconsistencies; no evidenced diversion or minority abuse.
gates.release_condition: Close prior compliance issues and provide correct auditor, related-party and loan particulars.

gates.reason: Complete FY26 notes, CARO and IFC are missing; material assets of₹130.1070crore are unclassified; FY25 IFC and contingency disclosures contain inconsistencies.
gates.release_condition: Provide the full signed, issuer-specific FY26 financial package and reconciled asset, cash, contingency and consolidation notes.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.reason: Available liquidity, current debt terms and obligations are not reconciled. Selected conservative model gaps are not evidence of actual default.
gates.release_condition: Authenticate free/restricted cash, deposit release and advance recovery, debt renewal/maturities, and a funded linked stress case.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Research hold, not an established compounder or a new-purchase recommendation. Neptune Pet is Neptune Petrochemicals Limited, a bitumen importer, trader and manufacturer, not a PET-packaging company. FY2026 sales reached ₹1,052.05 crore and reported standalone PAT ₹30.34 crore, but those headline numbers conceal commodity pass-through, non-operating income and a large change in supplier financing. The core investment question is whether the trading network can earn durable cash returns on the capital now committed. That is not resolved by a reported P/E around 13.24.

The decisive gap is ₹92.96 crore of other noncurrent assets and ₹37.14 crore of short-term advances without the detailed FY2026 notes needed to establish their nature, liquidity, restrictions and counterparties. Together they are 59.32% of assets and 76.35% of book equity. The filed annual report lists financial statements in its contents but omits them; the separately filed audited results supply statements but not the complete statutory CARO/IFC and notes. These are research limitations and disclosure inconsistencies, not proof of diversion or insolvency.

All three aggregate scores remain NS because material factors cannot be scored. G2 financial reliability and G3 funding are on hold; G1 is conditional and G4 is conditional on exceptionally limited execution capacity. No ordinary return, target or entry price is justified. A larger company, a long operating history and a sustainable road-maintenance need are positive facts, but neither substitute for reconciled capital and funding.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Information cutoff 20 October 2026; source retrieval 22 October 2026. Exact issuer Neptune Petrochemicals Limited, ISIN INE156901014, NSE SME symbol NEPTUNE, active normal series SM. Corrected listed CIN L24299GJ2021PLC126567 is confirmed by the 27 March 2026 filing; older reports use the prelisting prefix. Financial analysis uses standalone accounts so that earnings and cash have the same perimeter. FY2026 consolidated profit is ₹30.3339 crore, only ₹0.0051 crore lower, but the 51%-owned Revolv LLP is called an associate in results and a subsidiary in the annual report. That classification must be resolved before attributing all group liquidity or cash claims.

The last authenticated observed row is 15 October 2026 at ₹177.30, with 500 shares and one trade. The 19 October reference session has no issuer row; it is not treated as a zero-volume day or a fresh quote. The 500-share lot costs ₹88,650. A purely illustrative ₹500,000 position means either 5 lots costing ₹443,250 or 6 lots costing ₹531,900. This is not an allocation recommendation. Hurdle 15% nominal INR, pretax, five-year equity return; sensitivity 12% and 18%; entry 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031 is 1,826 days under actual/365.

Identity and historical source retrieval have high confidence. FY2023–25 core accounting and historical market observations are medium confidence after reconciliations; current asset classification, current liquidity and price-implied expectations are low confidence. Overall confidence for investability is low, the weakest material component. Full gate reasoning and release conditions are embedded below. Normal SM status does not establish historical surveillance membership, spread, depth or the ability to sell at a circuit.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The thirteen factors are assigned once and reused exactly. GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 5, CASH 2, EXEC 5, EARN 4 and D 4 are supported assessments. CAP, BAL, R, P and L are NS. REV uses the declared three-year reported growth basis, cross-checked against gross profit/value added. Both 14.12% revenue CAGR and 14.88% gross-profit CAGR fall in the score-6 band, without a trajectory adjustment. CAP is not rewarded for historical ROCE: plausible asset classifications move the three-year incremental-return diagnostic from 7.93% to 17.38%. BAL is not reduced to an invented low score merely because liquidity is unverified.

BQS uses GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL 8%, EXEC 8%. GQS uses REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15%, CASH 10%. IAS uses unrounded final BQS25%, R35%, D20%, P10%, L10%. Known-weight contributions, missing-factor 1–10 bounds, coverage and exact Decimal arithmetic are retained. None is renormalized or filled with 5. Scores are displayed with conventional half-up rounding only.

CASH 2 reflects four-year cash realization, dependence on liability timing and ageing, not only the final year's reversal. The raw missing-data GQS upper bound is therefore capped at 5 under the persistent-cash-quality override. GQS itself remains NS, not 5. There is no governance-failure override because serious minority harm or diversion has not been established. The numerical bounds are uncertainty diagnostics, not estimates or rankable scores. G2/G3 holds exclude favorable investment classification regardless of arithmetic.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The business sources bitumen, largely through import and trading channels, distributes it to road/infrastructure customers, and blends/manufactures bitumen emulsions and modified grades. Buyers care about specification, delivered price, reliable availability, credit and logistics. The economic spread is the margin between imported or purchased material and delivered product, after freight, handling, inventory risk, finance and credit costs. Revenue is recognized on goods supplied, not road-project value or announced government expenditure. Cash can move very differently from sales because suppliers, customer collections, deposits and advances finance the chain.

The current legal company was incorporated in 2021 after a predecessor business beginning in 2004. The FY2022 reported company row is a transition perimeter; full predecessor proforma sales were ₹556.79 crore, not ₹81.16 crore. Trading accounted for 75.28% of FY2023 revenue, 76.35% in FY2024 and 84.90% in 9MFY2025. Manufacturing tonnage is therefore an incomplete sales-volume measure. The reportable segment label manufacturing of bitumen does not make all revenue manufacturing.

The 2026 bio-bitumen license is nonexclusive for five years, with commercial scale and unit economics not established. Revolv LLP began with a tiny 51% subscription, not a major purchased revenue stream. Neptura Capital was incorporated in August 2026 with 75% ownership and a ₹75,000 subscription, nil turnover and proposed financing activity. No RBI authorization or profitable NBFC business is assumed. Future financial-services capital or credit risk is a monitoring issue, not an earnings contribution in this valuation.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
Network and procurement scale are the plausible advantages: import relationships, regional stocking/blending capacity and the ability to fulfil large time-sensitive orders can lower delivered cost and improve reliability. The evidence supports useful operating capability, not a proven enduring barrier. Three own manufacturing locations in the prospectus had modest utilization, and the commodity products are available through competing importers and refineries. A website claim of 11 network locations cannot be read as 11 owned plants; affiliated capacity and date matter.

Mechanism 1, distribution density: evidence is the multi-state plant/storage footprint and ₹1,052 crore sales; durability depends on freight economics and repeat procurement; failure mode is a competitor matching delivered price or sourcing. Mechanism 2, formulation/qualification: emulsions and PMB/CRMB require quality control, but BIS specifications and testing are industry requirements; failure mode is customer qualification of another supplier. Mechanism 3, technology: the bio-bitumen license adds optional capability, but nonexclusivity prevents a patent-monopoly thesis, and no proven commercial margin is disclosed. An entrant would need supply contracts, storage, logistics, testing and working capital; exact entrant cost/time and customer switching rates are ND.

Agarwal Industrial is the closest larger integrated bitumen/logistics comparator; its own shipping/logistics assets mean its economics and multiples cannot simply be transferred. Nexxus Petro is a closer small bitumen/blending comparator with overlapping modified products and its own bio-bitumen claims. HPCL/HINCOL compete with refining and nationwide distribution advantages, but are not pure-play equity comparables. The prospectus's FY2024 EBITDA margins were 3.04% for Neptune, 8.07% for Agarwal and 2.57% for Nexxus under its stated definition, an historical issuer-prepared comparison, not current peer valuation. No authenticated current peer multiple median is used. Neptune's nationwide market share with a consistent tonnage denominator is ND. Supplier concentration is more severe than customer concentration: the top three supplied 88.25% in 9MFY2025, and a March 2026 filing actually reports raw-material shortages and lower sales. This is concrete disconfirming evidence against assured supply superiority.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
The preferred comparable window is FY2023–FY2026 because five comparable audited annual intervals do not exist. Revenue ₹707.8229 crore to ₹1,052.0463 crore gives 14.1222% three-year CAGR. FY2024 declined ₹40.0851 crore; FY2025 added ₹280.2000 crore; FY2026 added ₹104.1085 crore. FY2026 growth 10.98% slowed from FY2025's 41.96%. Five- and ten-year CAGRs are ND. Four-year growth from the FY2022 combined predecessor proforma is 17.24%, context only; the misleading 772% growth from the partial FY2022 company base is not scored.

Gross profit/value added rose at 14.88% three-year CAGR, a useful economic cross-check rather than a replacement for revenue. FY2026 gross margin 6.99% versus 7.10% in FY2025 does not support an unqualified mix-upgrade story. Historical own-factory output fell 13.20% in FY2024, even while operating margins improved; trading drove most sales and its physical tonnage is unavailable. The 9MFY2025 manufactured share fell to 15.10%. FY2026 volume, realized price, product mix, imported versus domestic tonnage and constant-currency bridge are ND.

No material acquired revenue stream was found in the disclosed subsidiaries, so reported growth is not presented as acquisition-led. However, organic legal perimeter does not remove oil-linked price pass-through, FX and mix distortions. The declared REV basis is reported three-year growth, cross-checked against gross-profit/value-added growth under the same numerical schedule. Both measures fall in the 10–15% band, supporting REV 6 with Medium confidence and no trajectory bonus. Missing tonnage prevents a claim of volume-led growth, but does not by itself invalidate the consistent value-added evidence. H2FY2026 sales ₹645.47 crore versus ₹607.12 crore grew 6.32%, below the full-year rate; the March disruption limits straight-line extrapolation. No H1FY2027 result available by cutoff is invented, and the seasonal half-year is not annualized as TTM.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
India's road construction and recurring maintenance create an accessible use case, but a large national infrastructure budget is not Neptune revenue. Growth must come from tonnage delivered, reliable supply, regional economics and disciplined credit rather than simply more balance-sheet funding. Low historical plant utilization offers some throughput headroom; the rising trading share means new factory capex is not necessarily the binding constraint. The actual constraint may be import availability, deposits, working capital and customer collections.

The normalized operating NOPAT bridge rises from ₹9.7348 crore in FY2023 to ₹23.3002 crore in FY2026 at an analytical 25% tax rate. Keeping all noncash assets in a financing-side capital proxy yields only 7.93% incremental return; removing all ₹92.96 crore of current other noncurrent assets as hypothetical liquid nonoperating assets lifts it to 17.38%. Neither classification is authenticated. Against a reasoned 12–16% nominal INR cost-of-capital range, this uncertainty changes the investment conclusion. CAP remains NS because capital composition and price/mix are unresolved, not merely because project cohorts are unavailable.

Shareholders approved moving ₹4.5627 crore of planned plant expenditure to working capital in September 2026 after the disruption. Office capex had already been reduced and working-capital deployment accelerated, with ₹17 crore originally budgeted for FY2027 used during FY2026. These are disclosed reallocations, not automatically misuse, but they weaken an expansion-led earnings forecast. The license, Revolv and proposed financing business are options requiring separate economics and capital approval. GQS is NS, with a diagnostic ceiling 5 for persistent weak cash realization. A credible runway would require improving funded turnover and cash profit per share, not merely a higher sales target.

sections.title: Management Governance and Execution
sections.text:
The Shah family controls the business; the three disclosed promoter-director holdings total 15,274,950 shares, 67.43% of the 22,653,500 issued shares at March 2026. This is not claimed to be the complete current free-float reconciliation. FY2025 related-party sales to Riddhi Enterprise were ₹53.8988 crore, 5.69% of revenue, with ₹7.5979 crore receivable. Directors' remuneration totaled ₹0.866 crore, 3.45% of PAT. These are disclosed transactions, not proven non-arm's-length dealings. The H2FY2026 XBRL table separately shows ₹2.6943 crore related-party sales and ₹0.5267 crore Revolv loan balance; H2 values are not mislabeled full-year.

Governance concerns are specific. The prospectus disclosed erroneous incorporation-transition financial filings, a private-placement dematerialization noncompliance with adjudication requested, and delayed statutory filings. Closure evidence was not found. The FY2026 secretarial report records four exceptions: designated-person trading-window freezing not performed in September 2025; auditor appointment disclosure incomplete; shareholder approval of a casual vacancy delayed beyond three months; and incomplete particulars in a Section 185 loan-resolution explanatory statement. Its separate structured-database audit says all 14 required events were captured, positive counterevidence. The generic directors' statement that there were no qualifications does not override those exceptions.

Piyush J Shah resigned in July 2025 citing other assignments and no reporting dispute. MAAK resigned in August 2026 at the board's request for administrative/business convenience, explicitly denying audit, ethical or information-suppression concerns; Ashish Sheth was appointed and approved at September AGM. Two changes merit monitoring but are not a fraud conclusion. The current August-to-September approval must not be assumed to be the earlier delayed approval mentioned in the secretarial report.

Promises versus delivery: the IPO funded substantial working capital and most office expenditure, but plant deployment and office completion slipped; CARE reported no unsupported automatic funding surplus and noted schedule changes. September reallocation was shareholder-approved and explained by supply disruption. Revenue scale and disclosed responses support EXEC 5, while delayed assets, incomplete financial annexures and compliance repetition constrain GOV 4. July's machine-readable refile addressed the exchange's formatting query; it is not portrayed as an unresolved filing default.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2026 operating EBITDA is ₹31.7972 crore, 3.02% of sales, after removing ₹11.0887 crore other income. The management-style EBITDA₹42.8859 crore includes that income. Normalized PAT excluding all other income at 25% tax is ₹22.0679 crore versus reported ₹30.3390 crore. Other income is 27.37% of PBT and includes FX, interest and investment effects; excluding it all is a conservative operating-earnings definition, not a claim it has no economic value. FY2025 disclosed FX gains ₹8.4348 crore and interest ₹2.0481 crore illustrate the issue. FY2026 PAT grew 20.87% but weighted reported EPS fell 10.24% from 15.62 to 14.02 because of issuance/timing; current-issued-share EPS is 13.39. Share expansion 36.03% and old-holder ownership dilution 26.49% are different measures.

FY2023–FY2026 CFO totals ₹4.1773 crore against PAT₹86.6051 crore, 4.82% conversion; before-financing-interest cash-capex FCF proxy totals−₹2.9862 crore. Using the alternative FY2024 RHP cash series gives 3.28%, the same qualitative conclusion. This is not merely a negative final year: FY2023 CFO was−₹6.89 crore, FY2025 cash benefited ₹45.44 crore from supplier/other-liability changes, and FY2026 reversed ₹105.12 crore of those balances. FY2025 receivables older than one year were ₹9.7808 crore, 14.42% of the total, with no doubtful-debt provision. The contrary fact is that FY2024/FY2025 CFO was positive and FY2026 receivables/inventory declined; the cash weakness is not proof that all earnings are fictitious.

The FY2026 CFO receivable release ₹28.4148 crore exceeds the balance-sheet decline ₹23.1503 crore by exactly ₹5.2645 crore, offset by the CFS FX deduction. This reconciles, rather than becoming an invented accounting accusation. The ₹92.1255 crore investing outflow is labeled movement in other noncurrent assets, not capex; its asset movement/nature remains unprovided. The current P&L finance cost ₹1.6430 crore differs from cash-flow interest ₹1.6351 crore by ₹0.0079 crore. Small rounding/reclassification differences are retained, not conflated with the material missing notes.

FY2025 main opinion is unmodified; CARO states bank working-capital returns agree with books, no default and no reported fraud. However the IFC annexure names another issuer in its opening sentence and bears an inconsistent date, a template/issuer identity problem rather than substantiated ineffective controls. The main audit says no pending litigation while CARO/notes describe disputed dues. Notes show ₹0.2071 crore claims plus ₹1.8092 crore customs, yet repeat ₹0.2071 crore as total; recomputed ₹2.0163 crore is stress exposure, not admitted liability. CARO's customs amount is ₹1.75 crore; the ₹0.0592 crore difference needs reconciliation. Management says appeals/legal advice do not indicate material impact.

The audited FY2026 results opinion is unmodified. That does not replace the missing full statutory report, CARO, IFC, audit-trail annexures and asset notes in the annual filing. The funding bridge starts from ₹10.8933 crore reported cash, ₹18.9106 crore debt, ₹7.3393 crore March IPO unspent proceeds and known obligations, but deposit placement and the ₹130.1070 crore unclassified assets prevent confirmation of usable liquidity. All detailed history, definitions, alternative series, cash reconciliation and monthly conditional funding rows accompany this section.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the stale authenticated ₹177.30 reference, issued equity value is ₹401.6466 crore. Reported P/E is 13.24 and book multiple 2.36; the standardized ex-other-income P/E is 18.20. Ordinary EV is ND because liquid nonoperating assets, restrictions and all group claims are unresolved. Diagnostic EV is ₹409.66 crore if all reported cash were free and ₹417.00 crore after reserving all March IPO unspent from reported cash; neither adds back the unidentified ₹92.96 crore. A low reported P/E is not evidence of a valuation margin of safety. As separate earnings/book cross-checks, normalized P/E is 18.20 and book value is ₹75.22 per share; a purely hypothetical 50% impairment of the unidentified assets reduces book value to ₹46.50, not a liquidation valuation or an asserted loss. Ordinary DCF and NAV are unscoreable because capital maintenance, asset nature, cash restrictions and group claims cannot be authenticated. The terminal EBITDA method is therefore a conditional operating diagnostic, not a substitute fair-value point.

The operating scenarios explicitly link sales, margins, working capital, tax, reinvestment, debt repayment, IPO-eligible uses and cash. Bear growth−5%, EBITDA margin 2%, terminal 6×; base 10%,3%,8×; bull 20%,4%,10×. These are analyst assumptions, not company guidance or peer-derived fair multiples. Baseline monthly funding, without recovery of unclassified assets or assumed refinancing, breaches a ₹3 crore reserve in all three cases. Additional liquidity required is approximately ₹32.70 crore, ₹11.95 crore and ₹1.74 crore, respectively. These are conservative model gaps, not observed defaults. Reserve 0/1/3/5 and debt-renewal tests distinguish assumption sensitivity from a factual solvency claim.

A separate hypothetical case releases ₹30 crore of other noncurrent assets on 1 April 2026, reducing those assets by the same amount with no terminal double count. This is an unverified liquidity condition, not a forecast or a rescue received by shareholders. Under it base and bull clear modeled cash floors, producing conditional five-year returns 5.67% and 26.79%; bear still breaches, so its return and entry prices remain null. No ordinary scenario IRR or buy price is reported. Conditional 12/15/18% hurdle entries are retained only for fully funded paths.

With 3% margin, 8× terminal EBITDA and that same unverified ₹30 crore release, the finite funded reverse solver requires about 22.11% annual sales growth from March 2026 to support a 15% shareholder hurdle. This is considerably above the historical 14.12% CAGR, and it is not a valid ordinary price-implied-growth score while funding is unknown. Sensitivities vary working capital against cash release, operating margin against terminal multiple, reserve against refinancing, and recurring capex against new-business capital. Monthly rows, solver bracket/residual and exact terminal reserve are embedded so that a favorable terminal value cannot hide a pre-entry cash trough.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
sections.text:
The permanent-loss path starts with a procurement interruption or adverse oil/FX move, compresses a thin gross spread, then ties up deposits and advances while customers delay payment. Supplier credit that once supported growth is unavailable or unwinds. Published profit can remain positive while cash obligations require fresh equity at a weak price. An impairment of only a fraction of the ₹130.11 crore insufficiently described assets could substantially reduce book-value support; no such impairment is presumed in the base evidence.

A second path is capital-allocation drift: extra capital into finance or new products without disclosed funding and returns could turn a trading operation into a more leveraged or credit-exposed business. A third is implementation loss: one-sided SME trading or a price band can prevent exit regardless of spreadsheet value. At observed median turnover, even 10% participation does not accommodate one 500-share lot per session.

Disconfirming evidence is important: audited results remain profitable, FY2026 revenue and operating EBITDA grew, debt is modest relative to reported equity, no actual default was established in reviewed filings, and the unexplained assets may prove to be good recoverable deposits. A reconciled releaseable-deposit schedule could improve funding materially without issuing shares. Therefore the classification is unresolved hold, not evidenced distress. Bear financial outputs remain conditional diagnostics, and a negative cash line is not carried into a falsely investable IRR.

sections.title: Five Times and Ten Times Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold terminal share prices from ₹177.30 would be ₹886.50 and ₹1,773.00 before dividends or taxes, corresponding to equity values ₹2,008.23 crore and ₹4,016.47 crore at unchanged shares. Such outcomes require operating scale, margins, reinvestment and per-share ownership to work together; a terminal multiple alone is not a thesis. The detailed algebra shows sales required at 3% operating EBITDA and 8×/10×valuation, with a separate 10% ownership-dilution test. It deliberately does not pretend those revenue levels are funded solutions.

The fully linked solver finds no adjacent funded bracket for either 5× or 10× within tested−10% to 100% growth even with the hypothetical ₹30 crore asset release. Fast growth consumes working capital before enough cash accumulates; reporting the top growth endpoint as a solved requirement would be wrong. Additional financing, a fundamentally better net-working-capital model or much higher durable margins would be needed and would change ownership/risk.

The historical evidence does not establish a proprietary high-margin product, exclusive license, network lock-in or cheap unlimited reinvestment capacity. Existing factories have headroom, but the business is mostly trading and has demonstrated supply disruption. These outcomes are mathematically imaginable, not presently underwritten or reasonably designated a compounder. Evidence that would change this assessment includes audited traded tonnage/value-added growth, sustained cash conversion and a verified low-capital expansion model.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before reconsidering investability, obtain the complete FY2026 statutory financial package and corrected issuer-specific IFC annexure, including CARO, audit trail and detailed notes. Require counterparty, nature, maturity, security, recoverability and restrictions for ₹92.9627 crore other noncurrent assets and ₹37.1443 crore advances; reconcile them to bank deposits and the ₹92.1255 crore CFS movement. Obtain a published current liquidity bridge including debt maturity/renewal, guarantees, lease/capital creditors, taxes and subsidiaries. A generic no-borrowings sentence cannot override audited ₹18.91 crore debt.

At each half-year, compare physical traded/manufactured volumes and realization with revenue, gross profit and operating EBITDA. Demand a recovery plan if EBITDA margin stays below 2.5% or reported growth is driven mainly by prices/other income. Watch receivables over one year, collections from related parties, the large advance balances and supplier/current-liability funding. Two comparable reporting periods of cash generation and declining aged exposure would be more persuasive than one quarter's release.

Track office completion promised by March 2027, exact remaining IPO deployment and the ₹0.005 crore office arithmetic discrepancy; seek closure of disclosed statutory exceptions and actual auditor tenure stability. For Neptura/Revolv, require funding caps, licenses where applicable, ownership, external liabilities and demonstrable economics before crediting earnings. Review the material March supply interruption for evidence of actual normalization, not merely omission from later narrative.

For market implementation, obtain a complete classified 60 session trading distribution, current lot and surveillance status, spread/depth and a realistic whole-lot exit route. Any change to the illustrative position requires recalculation. Thesis falsifiers are an adverse audit/advance impairment, undisclosed external guarantees, material new-business capital without cash backing, continued weak conversion, or sustained inability to procure and sell at an economic spread. This is a monitoring specification, not a claim that an automatic monitor has been scheduled.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Research hold due to unresolved financial reliability and current funding, with significant SME liquidity constraints. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS. No business-quality, growth-quality or investment ranking eligibility is asserted, and no compounder label is earned. This is not Avoid–governance because severe misconduct has not been substantiated, and not Speculative–distressed because actual unfinanceability has not been demonstrated.

For a prospective purchase, do not convert conditional modeled upside or reported low P/E into an ordinary entry price. First resolve the source and liquidity holds, then rebuild the complete valuation and whole-lot execution assumptions. For an existing holder, the first practical issues are evidence and exit capacity, not a mechanical stop at a theoretical fair value; this research has no knowledge of the user's holdings, risk budget or tax position.

A favorable change would require authenticated liquid-asset availability, consistent financial annexures, acceptable funded stress and evidence that revenue growth produces recurring per-share cash economics. A lower share price alone would not resolve those requirements. Conversely, formal evidence of default, diversion or material unrecoverable advances would worsen the gate classification rather than merely lower a discretionary score.

sections.title: Sources Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence comprises the FY2025 full annual report, the incomplete FY2026 annual filing, the prospectus/restated and predecessor proforma financials, refiled audited FY2026 results, monitoring reports, AGM voting, subsidiary/license/disruption disclosures, auditor resignation annexures, integrated XBRL and exact historical exchange data. Source IDs, URLs, retrieval dates, original-file hashes and locators accompany the financial extracts.

Facts, company explanations, analyst calculations and assumptions are kept separate. The ordinary official website returned an authorization/security page, and alternate primary filings did not supply the missing FY2026 notes. The retrieval gap does not imply the documents do not exist elsewhere. Current information after 20 October 2026 is not used to improve the investment conclusion. Structural peer webpages were retrieved later solely to understand product/competitive mechanisms; current peer prices are not imported.

Material open questions are the asset/deposit composition and cash restrictions, current financing maturity and renewal, full auditor annexures and corrections, exact related-party/advance recoverability, physical growth bridge, subsidiary consolidation policy and new financing-business capital. Numerical alternatives are preserved where audited versions differ. Model taxes, reserves, debt-repayment schedule, growth, margins, capital intensity and the hypothetical asset release are disclosed assumptions, not management forecasts.

summary:
Research hold, not an established compounder or a new-purchase recommendation. Neptune Pet is Neptune Petrochemicals Limited, a bitumen importer, trader and manufacturer, not a PET-packaging company. FY2026 sales reached ₹1,052.05 crore and reported standalone PAT ₹30.34 crore, but those headline numbers conceal commodity pass-through, non-operating income and a large change in supplier financing. The core investment question is whether the trading network can earn durable cash returns on the capital now committed. That is not resolved by a reported P/E around 13.24.

The decisive gap is ₹92.96 crore of other noncurrent assets and ₹37.14 crore of short-term advances without the detailed FY2026 notes needed to establish their nature, liquidity, restrictions and counterparties. Together they are 59.32% of assets and 76.35% of book equity. The filed annual report lists financial statements in its contents but omits them; the separately filed audited results supply statements but not the complete statutory CARO/IFC and notes. These are research limitations and disclosure inconsistencies, not proof of diversion or insolvency.

All three aggregate scores remain NS because material factors cannot be scored. G2 financial reliability and G3 funding are on hold; G1 is conditional and G4 is conditional on exceptionally limited execution capacity. No ordinary return, target or entry price is justified. A larger company, a long operating history and a sustainable road-maintenance need are positive facts, but neither substitute for reconciled capital and funding.
